voyage.name: Tareef Cycling Club
voyage.content: It was founded in 1982 and developed into an active group in August 2007 by a former Jordanian National Team cyclist. They provide fun active weekend cycling and hiking trips, supporting all levels of fitness all around Jordan.

voyage.name: Cycling Jordan
voyage.content: Offers tours and weekly trips to the Jordan Valley and Dead Sea.

voyage.name: Amman Citadel
voyage.content: A national historic site at the center of downtown Amman. Its history represents significant civilizations that stretched across continents and prospered for centuries, as one empire gave rise to the next. Settlement at the Citadel extends over 7,000 years.

voyage.name: Jordan Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: The museum hosts a small but interesting collection of antiquities from all over Jordan. Fragments of the Dead Sea Scrolls which used to be housed here are now being transferred to the new National Museum of Jordan (see below).

voyage.name: Temple of Herakles
voyage.content: Roman period remains.

voyage.name: Umayyad Palace
voyage.content: In the northern portion of the Citadel, it offers a great view of Amman.

voyage.name: Byzantine Church
voyage.content: Dating to the 5th-6th centuries.

voyage.name: Roman Theater
voyage.content: Built during the reign of Antonius Pius, 138-161AD, this impressive theater could seat up to 6,000 people. Next to it are a folklore museum and a popular culture museum which the entrance fee also covers. Next to it is the Odeon theater, a smaller theater built at the same time. There are two small museums (Folklore and Popular Traditions) to the right and left as you enter.

voyage.name: Roman Nymphaeum
voyage.content: A partly-preserved Roman fountain.

voyage.name: Ammonite Watchtower
voyage.content: A circular watchtower built by the Ammonite kingdom some time between 500-1000 BC.

voyage.name: Rainbow Street
voyage.content: Near the 1st Circle in Jabal Amman, this is an interesting area to walk around and explore, it is named after the old Rainbow Cinema which is now out of use, but the area has experienced a revival with many of the old houses being restored and put into use, in the area there are some cafes and bars including Books@cafe and Wild Jordan, both with great views, a Caribbean restaurant, an Indian restaurant, a sushi joint

voyage.name: Darat al Funun
voyage.content: The 'small house of the arts' in Jabal el Weibdeh, overlooking the heart of Amman, is housed in three adjacent villas from the 1920s (and the remains of a sixth-century Byzantine church built over a Roman Temple), it has a permanent collection and also holds changing exhibitions. In the same area there are other small art galleries and the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts.

voyage.name: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
voyage.content: Situated in two separate buildings and in between a (open to the) public park of sculptures, it is showing international, contemporary art with a focus though on regional work.

voyage.name: The Jordan Museum
voyage.price: 5 JD (locals 1 JD, Jordan Pass is not valid)
voyage.content: This is a modern and well-preserved museum. Many of the artifacts from the citadel have been moved here. A great summary of Jordan's history. The entrance to the museum can be hard to find as the pedestrian entrance is sometimes closed so you must enter through the parking entrance. The current Google Maps location is slightly inaccurate: the museum and entrance are just south of the mosque.

voyage.name: Abu Darwish Mosque
voyage.content: Built in the 1920s by a private donor called Hasan Mustafa Sharkas and situated on a hill, this mosque impresses through its black and white striped walls.

voyage.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
voyage.content: Impressive new mosque, with a church opposite. Together, they give an interesting view.

voyage.name: Cave of the Seven Sleepers
voyage.content: These caverns are part of a Byzantine necropolis 10 km east of city centre. In legend they contained the Seven Sleepers, persecuted true believers hiding or immured here circa 250 AD, and emerging 300 years later to find Christianity the official religion, glory hallelujah. The same legend attaches to seven sites from China to Tunisia - Turkey has 3 - but this one is described in the 18th Surah of the Qu'ran and has

voyage.name: Royal Automobile Museum
voyage.content: A collection of cars, from the 100-year-old royal dynasty vehicles, to modern sports cars, to the Rover from the movie The Martian.

voyage.name: Wadi al-Seer
voyage.content: A region to the west of Amman, it is a small valley leading down towards the Dead Sea. Nearby is the al-Bassa Springs, the source of the valley's river. Above the spring is the al-Deir monastery. It's a 20-minute climb up to the monastery.

voyage.name: Iraq Al-Amir
voyage.content: 15 km from Wadi al-Seer, the , close to , are southwest of Amman and are great for a day tour.

voyage.name: Amman Waves Aqua Park and Resort
voyage.content: The biggest water park in Jordan (80,000 m²), opened in 2004.

voyage.name: Gilgamesh for Creative Arts
voyage.content: Art studio and cafe in a 1930s house. Hands-on workshops in pottery, Raku, Kurinuki, stained glass, glass painting, acrylic painting and Kintsugi (traditional Japanese repair with lacquer and metal powder), taught in English or Arabic. Sessions last about two to three hours and no experience is needed. Coffee, tea and snacks are included in the price. Booking in advance is recommended.

voyage.name: Pizza Roma Cafe
voyage.address: Amman Pasha Hotel, Al Shabsugh St 4

voyage.name: Shawermat Reem
voyage.content: The allegedly best shawarma in Amman is found in this street-side kiosk. It is very famous and there are even lines at 02:00.

voyage.name: Lebnani snack
voyage.content: This is a great place to eat Middle Eastern sandwiches, delicious ice cream and cocktails.

voyage.name: Hashem
voyage.price: For 3 JD per person (Oct 2018), you get the "mix" -- bowls of hummus, baba ghanouj, falafel, fuul, fries, salad and pita
voyage.content: During meal times, the place is swarming with locals and tourists. Wash this classic Arab meal down with a glass of mint tea.

voyage.name: Jafra Restaurant & Cafe
voyage.content: A quaint Lebanese restaurant that also offers pizza and shisha.

voyage.name: La Maison Verte
voyage.content: An impressive French restaurant, with excellent food and excellent ambience. A must go to place. Moderate to pricey, but it's worth it; the atmosphere alone is worth it, it's quite fancy yet very cozy. Their house specialities include "Entrecote", various steaks and a variety of sea food.

voyage.name: Levant
voyage.content: A very comfortable restaurant with excellent service, excellent English and excellent food. They serve "gourmet" Arabic food, which means fresh local ingredients in surprising and delicious combinations. For more information you can view their website.

voyage.name: Cantaloupe
voyage.content: A fairly trendy restaurant and cocktail bar with terrace impressively overlooking the city. Salads and fish are good, steaks are excellent. Regional and local wines are remarkably good. Service is excellent and unobtrusive. A little loud as the evening progresses.

voyage.name: Fakhr al Din
voyage.content: A real classical of Amman's Lebanese-oriented restaurant. Quite pricey but worth it, especially if you're in the terrace on a warm evening. For local wine, try their "Gerasa" red wine. Reservation highly advised. Great place, but beware of waiters who deliver unordered food to your table. Don't accept anything you don't order.

voyage.name: Sufra
voyage.content: It serves traditional Jordanian and Bedouin food with some more modern stylings. The restaurant is located in a traditional Jordanian villa with beautiful garden seating. Garden seating will likely require advance reservations. The food is more expensive than you can likely find elsewhere but is well-known, and is known for being a frequent favourite of the Jordanian Royal Family. Though, travellers have also been kn

voyage.name: Noodasia
voyage.content: Nothing to do with Arabic food, as the menu handles the whole map of Asia, from Thailand to China, through Japan (good sushis) and Indonesia. Nice place, excellent service and good food for the money, but no alcohol served.

voyage.name: Kan Zaman
voyage.content: Impressive medieval castle on a hilltop turned into a beautiful restaurant. The place is worth the visit. The food is pretty basic but ok. Ask for their local "Kan Zaman" red wine. Hopefully, the prices are not proportional to the size of the hall.

voyage.name: Picadelli Pub
voyage.content: Friendly place that serves alcohol, food, and complimentary snacks

voyage.name: La Calle
voyage.content: This multi-level bar is known for its half-price happy hour specials.

voyage.name: Jafra Café
voyage.content: A great spot right in the heart of the downtown area. It has an old, rustic feel to it with more young locals than tourists. They have a great selection of nargileh (water pipe) and the entire menu is reasonably priced. Expect to pay about 10 JD for dinner, including an appetizer, kebab, fresh juice and nargileh. Live music starts at 21:00 most night. There is another one near Paris circle in Jebel Al Webdeh.

voyage.name: Maestro Bar
voyage.content: Jazz and pub. There have been complaints about their entry policy.

voyage.name: Al-Mawardi
voyage.price: 5 JD for a coffee and hookah
voyage.content: Coffee shop with traditional hookah, a wide selection of coffee and beverages. Offers Backgammon boards but no card games.

voyage.name: Cliff Hostel
voyage.content: An option for low budget travellers. In the winter it can get very chilly, make sure that you ask for more blankets. Sometimes they heat your room if you ask for that.

voyage.name: Farah Hotel
voyage.content: Good backpacker option, has common area with satellite TV & movies, organises tours & very friendly English speaking staff.

voyage.name: Jordan Tower Hotel
voyage.price: From 9 JD incl breakfast and free WiFi
voyage.content: Shared trips at reasonable rates to all tourist sites. Dorm rooms male & female - 2-, 3- & 4-bed rooms some with ensuite bathroom and air conditioning and satellite TV. Friendly English-speaking staff. Cheap light snacks and airport pick ups.

voyage.name: Sun Rise Hotel
voyage.price: Dorm from 3.50 JD, different rooms available from 8-20 JD (depending on the mood of the manager, so take care)
voyage.content: One-star hotel with good location near Abdali station. Safe area, near Capitol Police Center. TV, free internet, free WiFi and air cond or fan in the room; rooms are very basic, those in the back are colder.

voyage.name: Sydney Hotel
voyage.price: 10 JD for a single, 14 JD for a double. Breakfast is 2 JD
voyage.content: Nice people, clean and safe.

voyage.name: Normas Hotel
voyage.price: 10 JD for a single, 12 JD for a double
voyage.content: Super friendly and helpful, clean and safe.

voyage.name: Zidian Hotel
voyage.content: Wi-Fi, hot shower, great view from the rooms on the back side.

voyage.name: Palace Hotel
voyage.price: 30 JD (with shower & satellite TV), 18 JD (shared facilities) for a double with breakfast included

voyage.name: Abbasi Palace Hotel
voyage.price: 6 JD for a dorm, incl. breakfast
voyage.address: Saqf Al Sail at Quraysh st
voyage.content: Clean and well-run. Good staff, knowledgeable and helpful. Price includes breakfast. Free Wi-Fi and internet. Free tea.

voyage.name: Amman Castle Hotel
voyage.content: Seems to be more catered to males and locals

voyage.name: Amman Pasha Hotel
voyage.content: Organizes free walking tours of Amman, and paid group tours to Madaba, Mount Nebo, Bethany Baptism site, Dead Sea, and Jerash. Tours are open to non-guests.

voyage.name: Al Fanar Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Standard hotel with reasonable facilities. Wi-Fi in reception (3 JD/hour). Indoor swimming pool, restaurant (but no bar). You can easily take a taxi down the road to the Regency Palace if you want a bar. Taxi cost is less than 1 JD. Hot water can be a problem.

voyage.name: Beirut International
voyage.price: 70 JD, but you can get a discount
voyage.content: Good location, nice big rooms, including Middle Eastern breakfast.

voyage.name: Beity Rose Suites Hotel
voyage.content: In the progressive district of Shmeisani, next to the Royal Cultural Centre and the Amman Stock Market. Friendly hotel in an attractive setting.

voyage.name: Crystal Suites Hotel
voyage.content: Nice suites hotel in a prestigious area opposite to the Four Seasons and Sheraton, comfortable for short and long stays, mainly one and two bedroom suites, some studios

voyage.name: Gardenia Hotel
voyage.content: Friendly hotel in nice and very quiet neighbourhood

voyage.name: New Park Hotel
voyage.content: Two-star hotel offering rooms with en-suite bathrooms, satellite TV, air-con, and central heating.

voyage.name: Gallery Guest House
voyage.content: Nice small hotel in a good location, only a few meters to the old center. The host speaks English and takes care of his guests. Roof terrace for the evening, WiFi, air conditioning and airport shuttle.

voyage.name: Bristol Hotel
voyage.content: Very good hotel if you can put up with the ever present smell of cigarette smoke (even in the non-smoking rooms). Wireless internet works well.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Amman
voyage.content: A wonderful luxury hotel.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Amman
voyage.address: Hussein Bin Ali Street, Jabal Amman
voyage.content: A favourite of the expat set for its laid back ambiance, terrace views and quality restaurants.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Amman
voyage.content: Another hotel popular with foreign professionals.

voyage.name: Kempinski Amman
voyage.content: All the luxury of a 5-star with interesting modern art features in the designer building.

voyage.name: Regency Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Popular 4-star hotel. Some areas need updating, but rooms are comfortable. There is a very good breakfast buffet. Internet access is available in the rooms.

voyage.name: Sheraton Amman
voyage.content: Another five-star.
